title: Almost 400 special bus permits granted ahead of ASEAN long-weekend rush
summary: Buses with routes all over Luzon and Western Visayas were granted special permits to ensure sufficient supply during the holiday.

blocks.text: Passengers bound for southern Luzon flock to the Cubao Bus Terminal on March 28, 2026

MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board issued special permits to 372 passenger buses in anticipation of an influx of passengers traveling during the five-day long Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit break.

Northern Luzon routes received the most permits with 245 units, followed by Central Luzon routes at 111 buses. The remaining 16 permits were granted among buses bound for Bicol, Southern Luzon and Western Visayas.
Bus stations along the Epifanio de los Santos Avenue Busway were also inspected ahead of the long weekend, following directives from Malacañang to ensure continuous operation during the break.

The Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange saw fewer travelers heading to the provinces for Undas this year as many chose to wait for the ASEAN Summit on November 16 to 18, which has been declared a special non-working holiday in Metro Manila.

Heightened security protocols during the duration of the summit. Travelers have been advised to plan ahead in light of disruptions including flight cancellations and schedule adjustments, road closures and traffic advisories.
